(ii). Post-Delivery: 
I. Following delivery without complications, mothers are permitted to travel after forty-eight (48) hours of delivery till seven days from delivery, provided they obtain a medical/fit to fly certificate from their treating obstetrician.
II. After seven (7) days following normal delivery and in the absence of any complications, such Passengers can travel without any restrictions. 
III. Passengers are permitted to travel seven (7) days after a caesarean/complicated delivery, provided such Passengers obtain a medical certificate and/or MEDIF/MEDA clearance certificate from AIXL doctor is mandatory and submit it at the check-in counter of AIXL.
(e). Carriage of Persons with Disabilities: Passengers with disabilities are mandatorily required to fill-up and submit the MEDA form at-least forty-eight hours prior to the scheduled time of departure.
(i). Paraplegic and Quadriplegic Passengers: For safety reasons, AIXL shall, take into account special assistance requirements, carry any number of paraplegic and quadriplegic Passengers as it determines in its sole discretion; however no more than four (4) quadriplegic Passengers per flight are allowed, or as otherwise provided in CARs. Under certain circumstances, we may require the Passenger to travel with a companion. Please refer to Article IX(e)(vi) (Travel with a Companion) for further details. AIXL may, despite its best efforts to accommodate all such persons, deny bookings, if the maximum number of such persons on a particular flight has been reached.
 
(ii). Mobility Devices: We accept mobility devices (only non-spillable battery-powered mobility devices) on our flights, subject to Article IX(e)(v) below. Passengers are requested to contact us at least forty-eight (48) hours prior to the scheduled time of departure of their flight to enable us to make arrangements for the carriage of battery-operated mobility devices. Failure to notify us may result in refusal of the carriage of the mobility device(s). We have provided more information on the transportation of mobility devices on AIXL Platform. Please also refer to the terms in Article X(g)(iv) for further details. 
(iii). Medication: Passenger/s with medical conditions /illnesses, including those that may require administering or carrying medication/ syringes on board the flight is required to contact AIXL at least forty-eight (48) hours prior to the scheduled time of departure of their flight to make arrangements for the type of special assistance required. Further, if you are travelling with an internal medical device, such as a pacemaker or a defibrillator, kindly inform AIXL at least forty-eight (48) hours prior and also while at the airport, to the security personnel conducting your screening, before the process begins. External portable medical electronic devices such as portable oxygen concentrator (POC), continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) device, nebulizer etc. may be used during all phases of the flight provided it does not interfere with the aircraft’s electrical, navigational, or communication equipment, or poses any safety hazard to aircraft, Passengers and/or crew. 
(iv). Medical condition and illness: Unless otherwise determined by us, Passengers with a medical condition or other illnesses are required to produce a valid medical certificate dated no more than ten (10) days prior to the date of travel and sign an Indemnity Form upon check-in at the airport (web-check-in in such instances is not available). For the safety of other Passengers, we reserve the right to deny boarding to any Passenger suffering from infectious, contagious, or chronic diseases and certain other medical conditions at our sole discretion (and if we decide that such condition may affect the safety of the Passengers while on board an aircraft).
While we make best endeavours to strictly enforce the above requirement and take all precautions in accordance with Applicable Law, all Passengers must note that there could be a risk of catching a contagious disease from other Passengers on the flight and, subject to Applicable Law, you agree to disclaim and not hold AIXL responsible for any, direct or indirect, health issue/ Damage that you may suffer on account of any disease or illness suffered during your flight. 
(v). Wheelchair facilities: Passengers requiring a wheelchair service are requested to pre-book wheelchair at the time of Booking and at least forty-eight (48) hours prior to the scheduled departure time of their flight. Failure to notify us in advance may result in any special assistance or wheelchair service being unavailable upon your arrival at the airport and you being refused carriage except as required by Applicable Laws. To avoid hassle or any delay, the Passengers with specific requirements are required to be present at the check-in counters at least two (2) hours prior to the scheduled departure time. Whilst AIXL makes its best effort to help Passengers to reach in time for their onward flight, Passengers are requested to be aware that there might be a delay in assisting them during peak flights arrivals/any other ground situation. AIXL shall not be liable to Passengers, who miss their onward flights if there is any such delay. Passengers are advised to consider such unforeseen delays and keep sufficient time gap while making their travel plans. Whilst AIXL makes its best efforts for wheelchair assistance, however, provision of a wheelchair is subject to available inventory.
(vi). Travel with a companion/safety assistant: We may require a Passenger to travel with a companion/safety assistant if:
a. it is determined essential for safety purpose under Applicable Law;
b. the Passenger is unable to assist in his/her own evacuation from the aircraft due to a mobility restriction; or
c. the Passenger is unable to understand or respond appropriately to safety instructions. Passengers with severe hearing, vision impairment and speech impairment (all together), if the Passenger cannot establish some means of communication with the cabin crew that is adequate both to allow transmission of the regulatory safety briefing, and to enable the Passenger to assist in his or her own evacuation of the aircraft in the event of an emergency; or 
d. Passengers with reduced mobility; or
e. Passenger travelling in stretcher: In this case, safety assistant or companion must be a medical/ paramedical person. AIXL may permit a Passenger to travel with a non-medical safety assistant in emergency cases upon production of medical opinion of Passenger’s doctor; or
f. Passenger has medical conditions including but not limited to psychiatric or emotional disorders, neurological disorder. However, AIXL reserves the right to allow Passengers with medical condition to travel alone upon production of medical opinion/certificate of Passenger’s treating doctor.
g. the Passenger has a disability, which AIXL, at its sole discretion decides, may affect the safety of the Passenger or other persons, while on board an aircraft.
Where such a Passenger is assisted by companion/safety assistant, we shall make all reasonable efforts to give such a person a Seat adjacent to such Passenger, subject to availability. However, AIXL shall endeavour to provide Seat to the safety assistant/companion in the row immediately in front of or behind the Passenger.
Safety assistant/companion in such case shall be an Adult. Further, safety assistant/companion must be physically and mentally able-bodied person who assists the above-mentioned Passenger(s) to exit the aircraft if there is an emergency evacuation, or to establish communication with the cabin crew for the required safety briefing. 
(vii). Seating for Persons with Disabilities: We will make reasonable seating accommodations for Passengers with specific requirements in accordance with Applicable Law and keeping in mind their safety and convenience. We will also make our best efforts to allocate you convenient Seats and provide you with all relevant and available assistive devices. We reserve the right to re-assign Seats at any time, including after boarding of the aircraft, as may be necessary for operational, safety, health, or security reasons. Restrictions on specific Seat assignments may also be applicable. Our crew will brief you before take-off on the emergency procedures, cabin layout and specialized equipment on the board to cater to your needs.
(viii). Service animals: Acceptance of carriage of service animals (i.e., trained guide dogs or ‘seeing eye’ dogs) in the cabin is subject to conditional acceptance. Passengers are requested to contact us at least forty-eight (48) hours prior to the scheduled time of departure of their flight to make arrangements for the carriage of such service animals. Our acceptance for carriage of such service animals is subject to the condition that (a) the Passenger assumes full responsibility for such animals, and (b) service animal is adequately trained, harnessed, muzzled, and vaccinated. AIXL shall not be liable for injury to or loss, delay, sickness, or death of such animal during or in connection with the carriage, including, in the event that it is refused entry into or passage through any state or territory.
X BAGGAGE (a). Baggage is designed to protect its content. Please note that your Checked-in Baggage may show signs of wear and tear as a result of normal Baggage handling. You are therefore advised to use Baggage that is of a suitable strength and durability to withstand such handling.
(b). Prohibited Items: AIXL reserves the right to refuse carriage of Checked Baggage and/or Cabin Baggage in the event the following items are found in such Checked Baggage and/or Cabin Baggage:
(i). improperly packed items in suitcases or other suitable containers, in order to ensure safe carriage with ordinary care and handling; 
(ii). items which are likely to endanger the aircraft or persons or property on board the aircraft and/or defined as dangerous goods under (i) the Dangerous Goods Regulations of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), the International Air Transport Association (IATA), any other regulations under the local civil aviation authority; or (ii) these Conditions of Carriage;
(iii). items which are prohibited for carriage by Applicable Law, regulations, or orders of any state to be flown from, to or over; 
(iv). items which contain irritants or incapacitating substances such as mace (spray), pepper sprays, etc.; 
(v). items which in our reasonable opinion are unsuitable for carriage by reason of their weight, shape, size, or character. Note that jackfruit and any other pungent-smelling fruits or items emitting foul smell are not allowed in cargo;
(vi). self-heating meals and beverages with flameless ration heaters;
(vii). perishable items (accepted in cargo and Checked Baggage only, at the sole discretion of AIXL);
(viii). Fragile items, live or dead animals; 
(ix). live plants (accepted in cargo and, upon proper packing, in Cabin Baggage, at the sole discretion of AIXL);
(x). human remains (only accepted in cargo) except in certain circumstances; 
(xi). fresh or frozen seafood or other meats provided that such items may be carried on board as Cabin Baggage only if we are satisfied that they have been properly packed. Strictly only Styrofoam and/or cooler boxes that contain dry food/non-perishables are allowed to be checked-in after inspection of contents by relevant authorities. Should a Passenger refuse inspection, we have the right to reject acceptance/admission of Baggage; 
(xii). firearms and ammunition, except on our selected Routes and under special circumstances and with prior permission of the relevant authorities (please see Clause X(c) below); 
(xiii). explosives, flammable or non-inflammable gas (such as aerosol paints, butane gas, lighter refills), refrigerated gas (such as filled aqualung cylinders, liquid nitrogen), flammable liquids (such as paints, thinners, solvents), flammable solids (such as matches, fire lighters), organic peroxides (such as resins), poisons, infective substances (such as viruses, bacteria), radioactive material (such as radium), corrosive materials (such as acid, alkali, mercury, thermometers), certain inorganic substances and powders (such as salt, sand, talcum powder), magnetic substances, oxidizing materials (such as bleaches), electronic cigarettes;
(xiv). weapons such as antique firearms, swords, knives, and similar items, provided that such items may be allowed as Checked Baggage at our sole and absolute discretion and only for special reasons. These cannot be carried into the aircraft cabin for any reason whatsoever; and
(xv). any other item prohibited to be carried on-board, as may be notified by Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS) or any other relevant authority.
(c). Carriage of Weapons and Ammunition:
(i). Passengers are not permitted to carry arms and/or ammunition on person or in Cabin Baggage as per Applicable Law. Besides actual weapons, certain items that may be misused as weapons or resemble weapons are also prohibited from being carried in the passenger cabin.  (refer to the prohibited item list here.) Bringing a prohibited item, including to the passenger and their Cabin Baggage screening check point, without authorization, is a criminal offence and may result in legal actions. At the security checkpoint, if any such item is detected on a Passenger or in Cabin Baggage, legal action shall be initiated against such Passengers as per Applicable Law. The firearm/ammunition may be seized for investigation and if necessary, used as evidence during prosecution by law enforcement agencies.
(ii). Exception: Based on DGCA Permit No. 2026-AA/2026, a bonafide Passenger can carry one licensed revolver or pistol or shotgun and cartridges in quantities as specified in the arms license not exceeding 5 kgs gross weight in their Checked Baggage, after declaring them at the check-in counter in writing, and meeting all safety and security requirements prescribed by the appropriate regulatory authorities.
(iii). The process for carrying authorized or licensed firearm and/or ammunition in the Checked Baggage is as follows:
a. Carriage of firearm and/or ammunition must be voluntarily declared orally followed by a written declaration either (i) at the time of check-in, where Checked Baggage screening is done post check-in; or (ii) before security screening of the Checked Baggage, where such screening is done prior to the check-in. Failure to declare such arms/ammunition may lead to criminal prosecution by law enforcement authorities.
b. Providing a valid firearms license or authorization for carriage of firearm and/or ammunition and other relevant documents is mandatory for declaration at the check-in counter and examination/verification at the relevant Baggage screening check point.
c. Firearms must be unloaded and packed separately from the ammunition. Ammunition should not be carried in loose form, and it should be in the proper package. The arms/ammunition must be so packed, protected and secured as to avoid the possibility of them being a source of danger.
d. If you are a sportsperson travelling to participate in any shooting event or relevant training and thereby carrying more than one licensed firearm and/or ammunition more than 5 kg gross weight, you must carry evidence to establish your identity and bonafide of such carriage of arms and ammunition. The evidence could be photo identity cards issued by a governmental agency or the sponsoring sports club, and a written document from the president or secretary of the sports club sponsoring you for the shooting event. Apart from these documents, authorization for carriage of firearms and/or ammunition by the sports persons in an aircraft shall be obtained from the DGCA in accordance with provisions of the Aircraft (Carriage of Dangerous Goods) Rules, 2003, as amended from time to time. Such documents will be verified by the security personnel.
(iv). A handling charge of INR 5500  (inclusive of taxes) or such other charge as may be informed by AIXL, per firearm and/or ammunition (subject to the Passenger carrying his / her valid arms and ammunition license as per the Applicable Law) per Passenger will be levied by us towards handling and carriage of firearms or ammunition in their Checked Baggage.
(v). The following personnel are exempted and will not be charged the above-mentioned handling charge provided they fulfil the following conditions:
a. Serving personnel from Indian armed forces, para-military forces and police, in each case, if travelling on duty and carrying an official movement order issued by their concerned department authorizing the carriage of firearms and/or ammunition for official purpose.
b. Sportsperson travelling for a competition or representing the country.
(vi). Please note that the policy for firearms and/or ammunitions may vary for other airlines. If you are connecting to any other airline, kindly contact them directly as they may have different/additional processes.
(d). Valuable and Fragile Goods: Passengers are strongly advised not to check-in valuable and/or fragile items as / in Checked Baggage. By checking-in such items as Checked Baggage, Passengers agree to bear the risk for the carriage of such items. The list of such items include, but are not limited to, money, jewellery, precious metals, silverware, electronic devices, computers, smart devices, cameras, video equipment, negotiable papers, securities or other valuables, passports and other identification documents, title deeds, artefacts, manuscripts etc. In the event such items are checked-in by the Passenger, it shall be at the sole risk of the Passenger, and AIXL shall not be liable for any Damage thereof for any reason whatsoever. AIXL assumes no liability or responsibility for any such items carried by the Passengers in their Checked Baggage (whether with or without AIXL’s knowledge), and such items are best hand carried. 
(e). Right to Search: For reasons of safety and security, AIXL, or any competent regulatory authority may require you to undergo a search, x-ray, or other type of screening on your person or your Baggage. We reserve the right to search your Baggage in your absence, if you are not available, for the purpose of determining whether you are in possession of or whether your Baggage contains any unacceptable or prohibited items. If you refuse to comply with such searches or screening, we reserve the right to refuse carriage to you and/or your Baggage without refunding your Fare and without any other liability towards you. Any other procedures as may be required under Applicable Law will be followed in relation to such cases. In the event that a search or scan causes injury to you or Damage to your Baggage, we shall not be liable for such injury or Damage unless the same is due to wilful misconduct or gross negligence on our part. We shall not be liable for locks/Baggage damaged due to security inspection at airport(s). In case the Baggage is spoilt due to spillage or leakage of bottles/jars unsuitably packed, breakage of any fragile items etc., AIXL will not be liable for such Damage.
(f). Delivery of Checked Baggage: Once a Baggage is checked-in, we shall take custody thereof and issue a Baggage Identification Tag (which may include a digital identification tag provided to you through SMS, WhatsApp facility on the contact details provided at the time of Booking) for each piece of Checked Baggage. Checked Baggage shall be carried on the same aircraft as you unless we decide for safety, security, or operational reasons to carry it on an alternative flight. If your Checked Baggage is carried on a subsequent flight, we shall make arrangements for you to receive your Baggage. It may be noted that you may be required to be present for clearance of Baggage.
(g). Checked Baggage: 
(i). Baggage fee shall be charged for the carriage of additional Checked Baggage and such fee shall be subject to change. Discounts may be applicable if excess Baggage is purchased at the time of Booking,. We may, at our sole discretion, also offer exclusive discounts or benefits to students, senior citizens, and the Indian armed forces personnel. 
(ii). Excess Baggage: Passengers may purchase excess Checked Baggage, subject to per piece restrictions. Discounts  may apply, if excess Baggage is purchased in advance, whereas full rates will be charged, if purchased at the airport check-in counters or ATO. In the event any Passenger checks-in a Baggage, and the weight of such Baggage exceeds free baggage allowance, the Passenger shall be required to make payment of excess Baggage charges at the airport check-in counter on the day of departure. Please refer to the link- Products and Services for details on all rates. The excess Baggage charges are non-refundable and non-transferable and are subject to change, unless the flight is cancelled by the AIXL, in which case, the AIXL will refund the excess Baggage charges collected. Further, excess Baggage charges will also be applicable on Connecting Flight. 
Note: Maximum weight for single piece of Baggage cannot exceed thirty-two (32) kilograms.
(iii). Any Checked or Cabin Baggage which exceeds the pre-booked rate shall be charged on a ‘per kilogram’ basis at the airport check-in counters on the day of departure. Please refer to the link Products and Services for details on all rates. Such charge is non-refundable and non-transferable unless: 
a. you are rerouted on to another flight under Article XI(b)(i), but do not receive the excess Baggage services that were purchased;
b. we have offered you a credit under Article XI(b)(ii) which includes the price paid for excess Baggage services; or 
c. we have offered you a refund under Article XI(b)(iii).
(iv). Baby buggies/prams, wheelchairs, mobility devices and walking frames: Such items are carried free of charge provided these items are used by Passengers in the course of travelling and have been notified to us as required by them, in accordance with these Conditions of Carriage.
Passengers are advised to make prior arrangements for their mobility device to be shipped by freight/cargo separately (subject to Applicable Law) if the mobility device (including battery powered wheelchairs) cannot fit through our aircraft cargo door (the dimensions of which are: 140 cm (length) x 140 cm (width) x 100 cm (height)), or cannot be carried on our aircraft due to any other local occupational health, safety and/or regulatory reasons. Wheelchairs powered by spillable (wet-cell) battery(ies) shall not be accepted since these batteries have corrosive acids and are considered to be dangerous goods. Electric powered wheelchair(s) with lithium or non-spillable battery or with batteries which comply with special provision A123 and A199 (as per current edition of IATA DGR Manual Chapter 4.4) or other similar mobility aids for use by Passenger whose mobility is restricted by a disability, their health or age, or a temporary mobility problem, shall be accepted for carriage as Checked Baggage subject to conditions. Passenger needs to seek prior approval from AIXL for the carriage. 
(v). Non-Transfer of Baggage allowance: A Passenger listed on the same Itinerary who does not travel cannot transfer their Checked Baggage allowance to other Passenger(s) on that same Itinerary.
(vi). For safety reasons the Carrier shall not accept any individual item exceeding 32 kilograms and with combined dimensions of more than 81 cm (height), 119 cm (width) and 119 cm (depth). This weight limit does not apply to mobility equipment (such as wheelchair). 
(vii). Out-of Gauge (OOG) baggage may be accepted subject to it being under the maximum dimension limits prescribed under Applicable Law and policies of AIXL in this regard.
(viii). Baggage like Sporting equipment/ Musical instruments/ Bulky fragile bags / Bicycle/ LED/LCD TVs 99 cm and above / Oversized Baggage (“Special Baggage”): The Special Baggage may be carried as part of the Checked-in Baggage upon payment of the fee set out in the Products and Services section and at your own risk. 
If the weight of the Special Baggage exceeds the Passenger’s permissible Baggage Allowance, then Excess Baggage charges as applicable will be levied over and above or the special equipment handling fee. Please refer to Products and Services section for details.
Any special baggage which exceeds our Cabin Baggage dimensions may be carried in the cabin provided it is within 22.5 kilograms and if a Seat for it has been purchased and the appropriate Fare paid (where policy in relation to extra Seats would be applicable). Please note that you will not be entitled for the Baggage Allowance associated with the purchase of an extra Seat for such purposes. 
We do not offer insurance option for the special baggage and you are recommended to obtain the same independently from a third party.
(ix). Carriage of Battery Cells: The carriage of battery cells in Cabin Baggage for any electrical / electronic items are permissible  and will not be removed at the security point. Spare / loose batteries, including lithium-ion cells or batteries, for portable electronic devices must be carried in Cabin Baggage only. For lithium metal batteries, the lithium metal content must not exceed 2g and for lithium-ion batteries, the watt-hour rating must not exceed 100Wh. The maximum number of such batteries to be restricted to 20 (twenty). Articles which have the primary purpose as a power source, e.g., power banks are considered as spare batteries. These batteries must be individually protected to prevent short circuits.
(x). Connecting Flight: Excess Baggage and/or any other relevant fees payable must be paid as point-to-point charges for both sectors at the point of origin, including extra Baggage handling charges. 
(xi). Collection of Baggage: You shall collect your Checked Baggage as soon as it is available for collection at arrivals. If you do not collect it within a reasonable time and the Checked Baggage needs to be stored at the airport premises, the airport operator may charge a storage fee. If Checked Baggage is not claimed within 30 (thirty) days, we may dispose it off without any liability or Damages payable to you. 
(xii). Baggage Dispute: Only the bearer of the Baggage Identification Tag delivered to the Passenger at the time the Baggage check-in, is entitled to receive such Baggage. If a person claiming the Baggage is unable to produce a Baggage Identification Tag or in case of any dispute as to the ownership of the Checked Baggage, we shall deliver the Baggage to such person who  has established to our satisfaction his right thereto, and if required by us, such person shall  indemnify us for any Damage which may be incurred by us as a result of such delivery, and will sign any documentation required by us in this regard. Acceptance of Baggage by the bearer of the Baggage Identification Tag without complaint at the time of delivery is prima facie evidence that the Baggage has been delivered in good condition and in accordance with the Terms of Contract between us. 
(xiii). AIXL is under no obligation to verify the identity bearer of the Checked-in Baggage and shall not be held liable for any  Damage arising out of, or in connection with its failure to do so. 
(xiv). If You Collect the Wrong Bag: If you pick up the wrong bag from the baggage carousel, it is your responsibility immediately to return the bag at your own cost to the baggage claims officer or airport manager at the airport where you collected it. You shall also be responsible for the cost of delivery incurred by us in delivering the bag to the rightful owner.
(xv). To ensure that the Passengers collect their own Checked Baggage only and that there is no confusion, we reserve all rights to do Baggage Identification Tag match upon arrivals either for all Passengers or on a random basis. In the event where there is a possibility or slightest assumption of a Passenger picking other Passengers’ Checked Baggage, we reserve all rights to divulge personal information of such Passenger to the Law enforcement authorities (in accordance with the Applicable Laws) and shall not bear any liability with respect to such disclosure. 
(xvi). Process of Reporting the Damaged/ Delayed/ Lost Checked Baggage: Acceptance of the Checked-in Baggage by Passenger without complaint at the time of delivery, is prima facie evidence of Checked-in Baggage being delivered in good condition and in accordance with the Conditions of Carriage. A Passenger shall be required to raise an irregularity report in case there is a loss of or Damage to Checked-in Baggage, while he/she is at the respective destination airport, at the time of arrival, and not after departing from the destination airport.
In the event a Passenger reports loss, Damage or pilferage of his/her Checked-in Baggage, a copy of duly filled Property Irregularity Report (“PIR”) along with requisite supporting documents, must be submitted at the relevant airport before exiting the airport. Failure to do so, will result in the rejection of any claim raised by a Passenger. Additionally, Passenger(s) must:
Confirm the number of Baggage pieces in Passenger 's possession;Confirm the weight of Baggage in Passenger 's possession, as against the weight reflected in the check-in record available in AIXL check-in system so as to ascertain the balance in weight which is the subject of the PIR.
a) Procedure for Claiming Lost Baggage / Items: The lost item (if found) may be claimed by the Passenger who should be in possession of the following documents:
Copy of the boarding pass;Copy of photo ID card issued by any government authority, preferably Passport / driving License / AADHAR Card; andDetails of the items being claimed. 
b) In case of an authorized person on behalf of the Passenger, they should carry the following documents:
Letter of authorization to collect the item on behalf of the Passenger;Copy of Boarding Pass of the Passenger;Copy of photo ID card of the Passenger issued by any government authority, preferably Passport / driving license / AADHAR Card; andPhoto ID card of the person who is authorized to collect the item.
NOTE: Item(s) must be collected within 7 days from the date of notification received from the Carrier. On expiry of 7 days, it is disposed of as per government directive and handed over to customs. Carrier will not be liable for any types of further claim.
(h). Cabin Baggage: 
(i). Passengers may carry only one piece of Cabin Baggage in compliance with Indian security regulations (ref. BCAS “One Hand Baggage Rule”, Circular 6/2000, dated 24 Feb 2000). Accordingly, the Passengers (except Infants) are allowed one (1) piece of Cabin Baggage to be carried on board. The Cabin Baggage shall not exceed the dimensions of 56 cm X 36 cm X 23 cm = 115 cms. 
The Cabin Baggage must fit under the Seat in front of you or in the overhead bin/compartment in the cabin. 
(ii). In addition to the one (1) Cabin Baggage as stated above, the Passenger may also carry one laptop bag not exceeding the dimension of 30 cm x 40 cm x 10 cm. The Passenger shall ensure that the total weight of the one (1) Cabin Baggage and the laptop bag combined does not exceed 7 Kgs, failing which AIXL will be entitled to charge excess baggage fee in accordance with Article X(h)(iii) below.
(iii). Any Cabin Baggage of excessive weight or size may be permitted on board the aircraft, subject to the baggage limits and upon payment of prescribed fee. Passengers are advised to check in such items as Checked Baggage at the airport check-in counters in accordance with Article X(f) and Article X(g) hereof, failing which, we reserve the right to check-in such Baggage as Checked Baggage upon boarding, subject to Baggage fee payable at the boarding gate (please refer to the Products and Services section). 
 
(iv). Liquids, Aerosols, and Gels: Subject to the prevailing Applicable Laws, Passengers may take certain liquids on board in their Cabin Baggage provided they meet the following restrictions: 
a. The liquid is in a container with a maximum volume of 100ml; and
b. That all liquid containers meeting the maximum volume of 100ml each can be fitted comfortably into a transparent, re-sealable one litre plastic bag. 
The plastic bag should be presented separately at security. You may be required to dispose of liquids, which do not meet the above requirements. 
(v). Items which cannot be carried in Cabin Baggage: Items such as the following will not be permitted to be carried on person or in Cabin Baggage. The list given below is not exhaustive and will be subject to Applicable Law.
(a) Personal Items- Lighters, scissors, metal with pointed tips, realistic replica of toy weapon.
(b) Sharp Objects- Box cutters, ice axes/ ice picks, knives (any length and type except round-bladed, butter, and plastic cutlery), meat cleavers, razor-type blades such as box cutters, utility knives, razor blades not in a cartridge, but excluding safety razors, sabers, sword.
(c) Sporting Goods- Baseball bats, bows and arrows, cricket bats, golf clubs, hockey sticks, lacrosse sticks, pool cues, ski poles, spear guns.
(d) Guns and Firearm- Ammunition, BB guns, compressed air guns, firearms, parts of guns and firearms, pellet guns, realistic replicas of firearms, starter pistols.
(e) Tools- Axes and hatchets, cattle prods, crowbars, hammers, drills (including cordless portables power drills), saws (including cordless portable power saws), screwdrivers (except those in eyeglass repair kits), tools (including but not limited to wrenches and pliers), wrenches and pliers.
(f) Martial Arts/ Self Defence Items- Billy clubs, black jacks, brass knuckles, kubotan, mace/ pepper spray, martial arts weapons, night sticks, nunchakus, martial arts/self defence items, stun guns/shocking devices, throwing star.
(g) Explosive Materials- Such as flare guns, gun lighters and gun powder, explosive material. blasting caps, dynamite, fireworks, flares (in any form), hand grenades, plastic explosives and realistic replicas of explosives.
(h) Compressed gases- Deeply refrigerated, flammable, non-flammable and poisonous such as butane, oxygen, liquid nitrogen and aqualung cylinders.
(i) Flammable Items- Such as aerosol (any except for personal care or toiletries in limited quantities), fuels (including cooking fuels and any flammable liquid fuel), gasoline, gas torches, lighter fluid, strike anywhere matches, turpentine and paint thinner, realistic replicas of incendiaries.
(j) Oxidizing materials- Such as bleaching powder, peroxides.
(k) Poisonous and infectious substances- Such as insecticides, weed-killers and live virus materials.
(l) Radio-active materials.
(m) Corrosives- such as acids, alkalis, mercury, wet cell batteries (except those in wheelchairs), oven or drain cleaners.
(n) Other dangerous articles- such as magnetized, offensive or any other articles which could cause inconvenience/ disturbance to co-Passengers or affect the safety of the Flight, including briefcases and attaché cases with installed alarm device; and
(o) Any other item as may be restricted under the Applicable Law and the regulatory guidelines issued from time to time.
(vi). Items Removed from Passengers by Airport Security Personnel: We will not be responsible for, nor have any liability in respect of, items removed from you or your Baggage by airport security personnel acting in accordance with Applicable Law, whether or not any such items are subsequently retained or destroyed by such airport security personnel or are passed on by such airport security personnel to us or third parties.
(i). Aircraft Weight Limitation: If the aircraft weight limitation is otherwise exceeded, we reserve the right to decide which items shall be carried on board.
XI CHANGES IN SCHEDULES, CANCELLATIONS(a). Schedules and Intimation: We will use our best efforts to avoid delay in the carriage of Passengers and their Baggage. We endeavour to adhere to published schedules in effect on the date of travel. However, times shown in timetables, schedules or elsewhere are subject to change at any time and from time to time. We are not liable in any way whatsoever for any loss/Damage incurred by Passengers as a result of such change. Passengers are required to ensure that they provide AIXL with their correct and updated contact details (including e-mail id and mobile number), so that we may communicate such changes in schedules to them. We shall not be liable for any liability or claim if Passenger(s) have not provided accurate and valid contact information at the time of Booking. Passenger(s) will also be provided a prior notification, if they are required to report to the airport check-in counter earlier than the prescribed time period, before the scheduled departure of the flight, on account of extra security measures or for any other reason. Passengers understand and acknowledge that if their phone number and/or email address is found to be incorrect or unreachable or if they cannot be contacted due to any reason whatsoever, AIXL cannot be held liable for the same. 
(b). Cancellation, Changes of Schedules due to Extra-Ordinary Circumstances: In terms of the applicable CAR, AIXL is not obliged to pay compensation or provide facilities, where cancellations and delays have been caused by an event(s) of Force Majeure, i.e., extraordinary circumstance(s) beyond the control of AIXL, the impact of which lead to the cancellation / delay of flight(s), and, which could not have been avoided even if all reasonable measures had been taken by AIXL. Such extraordinary circumstances may in particular, occur due to political instability, natural disaster, civil war, insurrection or riot, flood, explosion, government regulation or order affecting the aircraft, strikes and labour disputes causing cessation, slowdown or interruption of work or any other factors that are beyond the control of AIXL.
Additionally, AIXL would also not be liable to pay any compensation in respect of cancellations and delays clearly attributable to Air Traffic Control (ATC), meteorological conditions, security risks, or any other causes that are beyond the control of AIXL, but which affect their ability to operate flights on schedule. Extraordinary circumstances should be deemed to exist where the impact of an air traffic management decision in relation to a particular aircraft or several aircraft on a particular day, gives rise to a long delay or delays, or any overnight delay, or the cancellation of one or more flights by AIXL, and which could not be avoided even though AIXL had taken all reasonable measures to avoid or overcome the impact of the relevant factor and, therefore, the delays or cancellations.
Further examples / illustrative list of force majeure/extra ordinary circumstances:  Bandh or other similar shutdown, hartaal, strike, bird strike, and operating crew unable to reach due to congestion on roads or any other circumstances beyond their control, security congestion at airport terminals, delays in departure due to offloading/No-Shows, consequential delay due to late arrival of the incoming aircraft due to congestion or any other circumstances beyond their control, inclement weather / storm / cyclone, due to any restrictions from ATC / Airport authority / government authorities, etc. In the event of such circumstances, we shall at our discretion (except for the credit shell which shall be at the option of the Passenger), offer you one of the following options or any other option as per the Applicable Law: 
i. To provide carriage at the earliest opportunity on another flight on which space is available without additional Charge;
ii. To retain the value of your Fare in credit shell or voucher for your future travel if you choose to travel at another time, provided that you must re-book within the time then stated in our Terms of Contract with you; or
iii. To refund the value of your Fare to your original mode of payment if you choose not to proceed with your trip due to a flight cancellation, delay and/or rescheduling (i.e. preponed by 1 hour or delayed by three (3) hours or more) before the original scheduled departure time, or after departure time. Passengers may request for the desired service recovery free move flight change, or the full refund, two (2) hours prior to the scheduled flight departure time. 
(c). Cancellations for reasons other than extraordinary circumstances: 
AIXL will endeavour to inform the Passengers of cancellations at least two (2) weeks prior to the scheduled time of departure and arrange an alternate flight or refund as acceptable to the Passenger. In the event you are informed of such cancellation less than two (2) weeks prior, but up to twenty-four (24) hours of the scheduled departure time, AIXL shall offer an alternate flight or refund the ticket, as acceptable to the Passenger. 
Passengers who have not been informed as per the abovementioned timeline, or missed the Connecting Flight (i.e. booked on the same ticket number of AIXL), AIXL shall either provide an alternate flight as acceptable to the Passenger or  provide the following compensation in addition to the full refund of Ticket: 
(i) INR 5000 or booked one-way base fare plus airline fuel charge, whichever is less, for flights having a block time of up to and including 1 hour; or 
(ii) INR 7500 or booked one-way base fare plus airline fuel charge, whichever is less, for flights having block time of up to and including 2 hours; or 
(iii) INR 10000 or booked one-way base fare plus airline fuel charge, whichever is less, for flights having a block time of more than 2 hours. 
AIXL will (wherever reasonably permissible) provide free-of-charge meals and refreshments in the event the Passenger has reported for their flight and is waiting for an alternate flight. 
The Passenger understands and acknowledges that no further compensation (whether indirect, consequential, or remote) would be payable under any other head, in addition to the aforesaid compensation.  
No financial compensation shall be payable to Passengers who have not provided adequate contact information (email id or a phone number) at the time of making Booking or when the Ticket for firm travel on the selected flight is issued. In respect of such Passengers, AIXL will either refund the Ticket price or make reasonable endeavour to make alternate travel arrangements as per the choice of the Passengers. Additionally, in respect of such Passengers who elect to travel to their destination on an alternate flight, AIXL shall provide them with reasonable facilities during the period that they are required to wait at the airport for the alternate flight such as providing for meals and refreshments.
In the event that an alternate flight provided by AIXL is scheduled to depart from a terminal different from the one originally designated, AIXL shall arrange transportation to the appropriate terminal. This obligation shall not apply if the Passenger was informed of such terminal change at least six (6) hours prior to the scheduled departure time.  
(d). Flight Irregularities: If at any time after the Passenger has successfully booked a Seat, and the booked flight is delayed, cancelled, or there are changes to the schedule due to any reason whatsoever:
a. We shall at our option (and in accordance with Applicable Laws), take any of the following actions:
(i) provide the Passenger, subject to availability, the same Seat or a Seat of equivalent value on the next available flight, without any additional charges or extend the availability of the Booking;
(ii) provide the Passenger any randomly assigned Seat on the next available flight, whereby we shall then refund the Passenger the charges paid for the Seat selection;
b. Passenger at its option can: 
(i) retain the value of the Booking in a credit account for their future travel provided that the Passenger must re-book within three (3) months from the original date of travel; or 
(ii) refund the value of the Booking to the original mode of payment.
The options outlined in this Article are the sole and exclusive remedies made available to you and AIXL shall not be responsible for any Damages suffered by you in such an event, unless otherwise provided for in these Conditions of Carriage or under Applicable Law.
(e). Diversions: If your flight is diverted to a different destination, please contact our crew in case you have any queries. Our crew will be providing information and refreshments such as tea, coffee, water etc.  
(f). Connecting Flight: If a delay or cancellation/reschedule of our flight causes you to miss a Connecting Flight on which you hold a confirmed Booking and you have reported at the airport for your original flight departure time, you are entitled to the following:
i. If your flight is delayed at the point of origin – you will be moved to the next available flight that connects to the final destination within our Connecting Time, without any additional cost on your behalf.
ii. If your subsequent flight is delayed i.e., free move to the next available flight within our Connecting Time.
iii. If your new flight does not meet our Connecting Time or if the next available flight falls on the next day, we will provide the following:
1. Day or overnight accommodation;
2. Surface transfers; or
Any compensation in this matter shall be paid in accordance with the applicable CARs and AIXL’s liability shall be limited in accordance with the provisions thereof. Passenger understands and acknowledges that no further compensation (whether indirect or consequential or remote) would be payable under any other head, in addition to amounts prescribed as per the applicable CARs.
For Bookings involving 2 (two) or more Sectors under different PNRs, it is the Passenger’s responsibility to ensure that there is a sufficient time-interval between the two flights, as their carriage may be affected by factors beyond control including a change in aircraft, flight delays or cancellations, issues in relation to Baggage handling, operational issues or change in carriers at a stopover. If a Passenger misses their connecting flight due to such circumstances or factors arising from a preceding flight, AIXL shall not be liable for such missed connection, in any manner whatsoever.
Further, to refer to the latest copy of the Passenger Charter issued by the Ministry of Civil Aviation which provides the general guidance on the rights of the   passengers for air travel, please click here.
XII REFUNDS(a). Refund Policy: If you are entitled for a refund from AIXL in accordance with these Conditions of Carriage, it shall be done in the following manner:
Refunds for tickets purchased through the AIX Platform and Airport Ticketing Offices through Credit / Debit Cards, Net Banking, Wallets and other electronic means will be processed within 7 days from the day of cancellation by AIXL to the cardholder’s account.AIXL shall endeavour that the refund of any Ticket issued by a Trade Partner is processed within 14 working days. In the event of any delay in receipt of payment beyond 10 working days from the date of cancellations by the Trade Partner, Passenger should promptly inform AIXL of the same.In case of cash transactions, refund shall be made immediately by the AIXL’s ATO from where the ticket was purchased.AIXL shall refund all statutory taxes and user development fee (“UDF”)/airport development fee (“ADF”)/passenger service fee (“PSF”) to the Passengers in case of cancellation/non-utilisation of Tickets/no show.
(b). Person Entitled for Refund: A refund made under these Conditions of Carriage and our internal policies, shall be made only to either of the following persons:
(i). the person named or recorded on the Ticket as a revenue Passenger; or
(ii). the person who purchased the Ticket upon presentation to us of satisfactory evidence to prove that he/she is entitled to such refund.
(c). Tax Refunds: In the event of ticket cancellation, non-utilisation, or no-show, AIXL will refund all statutory taxes including airport tax, value-added tax (VAT) or goods and services tax (“GST”) paid on the airport tax and certain fees (including UDF, ADF, PSF). This refund will be applicable for all fare type (including promotional fares) and even where the base fare is non-refundable. The refund amount will be net of GST and must be requested in writing within one (1) year from the scheduled travel date. 
(d). Involuntary Refunds: For the purposes of this Article XII, the term ‘Involuntary Refund’ refers to a refund issued when a Passenger is unable to travel on a flight as booked due to circumstances such as: (a) flight cancellation by AIXL, (b) failure to operate a flight according to schedule beyond AIXL’s control or due to a Force Majeure event, (c) failure to operate a flight according to the schedule beyond a reasonable time, (d) failure to stop at Passenger's destination for any reason provided in Article XI(b),(e) failure to provide Passenger with a Seat in the flight booked by such Passenger for any reason provided in Article V(g)(ii), or (f) refuse to carry or remove Passenger pursuant to any of Article IX(a) (i), (ii), (iii), (iv), (v), (vi), (xiv), and (xv). In such event, the amount of the refund made available to such Passenger shall be:
(i). if no portion of the trip has been made, an amount equal to the Fare paid; or
(ii). if a portion of the trip has been made, the higher of the following:
a. the amount equal to the Fare paid for the untraveled portion, less the same rate of discount, if any, that was applied in computing the original Ticket Price applicable to the unused transportation from the point of termination of travel (or the point at which transportation was to be resumed in the absence of the termination) to the destination indicated or recorded on Ticket; or 
b. the difference between Ticket Price paid and Ticket Price for the Carriage completed. 
In the event the flight is cancelled due to a Force Majeure Event, we may also, at our option, make a refund pursuant Article XI(b)(iii). 
(e). Refunds for Reasons other than Involuntary Refunds: Unless otherwise required by Applicable Law or our terms and conditions, we will refund TFC related to air travel imposed by a government authority, or the airport operator or any relevant authority (including airport tax and GST paid on the airport tax) only for reasons not specified in Article XII(d). Such TFC are subject to following conditions: (i) only refundable if requested in writing within one (1) year from the date of travel, and, (ii) the refund will be net of GST.  
(f). Right to refuse Refund: Notwithstanding the provisions of this Article XII, we may refuse to grant a refund for Ticket in the event that:
(i). With regard to a Passenger’s Ticket presented to us or to Government officials of a country as evidence of such Passenger’s intention to depart such country, but fails to provide sufficient proof of having permission to remain in the country or plan to depart via another Carrier or other transportation service; or
(ii). Carriage of Passenger is refused or he/she is removed pursuant to any of Article IX(a) (vii), (viii), (ix), (x), (xi), (xii), and (xiii), provided, however if the Passenger pays part of the Ticket Price, and carriage of the Passenger is refused or he/she is removed in accordance with Article IX(a)(vii), we shall refund to the Passenger the money received from such Passenger.
(g). Refund Claim
i. Flight Cancellation: Passengers must submit any refund claims (if any) related to flight cancellations within one (1) year from the date the Booking was cancelled.
ii. No Show: In the event of a no-show, Passenger must submit refund claims (i.e. statutory taxes and airport charges) within a period of one (1) year from the scheduled date of departure.
XIII CONDUCT ON BOARD THE AIRCRAFT  (a). If in our reasonable opinion, any Passenger conducts himself at any time after entering the airport premises or at the time of boarding, including but not limited to pre-boarding or aboard the aircraft, in a manner so as to endanger the aircraft or any Passenger or property on board, or obstruct or hinder the crew or ground staff in the performance of their duties, or fail to comply with any instruction of the crew or is likely to behave in a manner that is disruptive and/or unruly, AIXL may take such measures as it deems reasonably necessary to prevent continuation of such conduct, including to decline boarding or require disembarkation, and to cancel the Ticket. 
(b). Disruptive or unruly conduct includes, but is not limited to: 
(i). behaving in an unruly, unsafe, or aggressive manner which is considered objectionable by AIXL; or 
(ii). assaulting, intimidating or threatening, (whether physically or verbally) a crew member which may interfere with the performance of the duties of the crew member or lessen their ability to perform those duties or any other person; or
(iii). damaging, destroying or interfering with the aircraft or its equipment; or
(iv). refuse to follow a lawful instruction given by the Pilot-in-Command, or on behalf of the Pilot-in-Command by a crew member, for ensuring the safety of the aircraft or of any person or property on board or for maintaining good order and discipline on board; or
(v). Failing to comply with any instructions or directions of the crew or ground staff, including but not limited to failing to cooperate or interfering with the crew member’s duties, refusing to follow instructions to board or disembark the aircraft, instructions with respect to smoking, alcohol, drug consumption, security and safety or use of an electronic equipment; or 
(vi). insulting the modesty of ground staff, crew members or other passengers or customers, uttering any word, making any sound or gesture, or exhibiting any object, intending that such word or sound will be heard, or that such gesture or object will be seen by others, or intruding and/or invading upon the privacy of ground staff, crew members or other passengers or customers; or 
(vii). committing the following acts of sexual harassment against ground staff, crew members or other passengers or customers – Physical abusive behaviour, through means of contact and/or advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures, inappropriate touching, groping etc., 
making sexually coloured remarks, attempt to disrobe, showing pornography, or demand or request for sexual favours; or 
(viii). behave in a manner which causes or is likely to cause discomfort, distress, inconvenience, damage or injury to other passengers, ground staff, the crew or property. 
(c). Carrier will have the right to offload such Passenger(s) and take the following measures as appropriate:
i. If conduct is at the airport: If a Passenger engages in a conduct as mentioned in XIII (b) above, AIXL reserves the right to refuse the carriage of such Passenger, cancel the Booking, or remove en-route unruly Passenger.
ii. If conduct is on board the aircraft: Any Passenger who engages in a conduct as mentioned in XIII (b) above, while on board the aircraft shall be subject to a disciplinary action. AIXL reserves the right to caution Passenger against such behavior initially. However, if the Passenger fails to comply with AIXL’s instructions, the pilot-in-command may immediately take appropriate action, which may include diverting the aircraft to the nearest available location and offloading the Passenger to prevent further disruption and for maintaining good order and discipline on-board. In the event AIXL divert the aircraft for the purpose of offloading the Passenger, the Passenger shall pay all costs resulting from that diversion.
iii. In addition to the above measures, for conduct at the airport or on board the aircraft, AIXL may also take the following remedial measures:
(a) Report the matter to the state police / law enforcement authorities for necessary action and such Passenger may face legal consequences, including but not limited to interim ban, arrest, imposition of fine and/or imprisonment as per the discretion of the enforcement agencies.
(b) Disruptive/unruly Passenger(s) may be placed on the No-Fly list and banned from flying for a specified amount of time as communicated to them, in accordance with law. 
(c) Passenger shall be held liable for any damages / losses (including the diversion / offloading costs) thereof and shall also be liable to compensate AIXL (and such other the affected person at the airport, or on-board aircraft) for all losses, claims, liabilities, cost and expenses suffered or incurred by AIXL (and such other the affected person at the airport, or on-board aircraft) in connection with or as a consequence of unruly act of the Passenger. Carrier shall not be held liable for any damage or loss arising out of the Passenger’s unruly behavior at the airport and/ or on board the aircraft or any cost incurred by him due to cancellation of the Booking or de-boarding him from the aircraft due to unruly act. In such circumstances, AIXL shall have no liability, and the Passenger shall not be entitled to any refunds. 
(d). For safety reasons and in certain circumstances, AIXL may forbid or limit operation on board the aircraft of electronic equipment, including but not limited to, cellular phones, laptop computers, portable recorders, portable radios, CD players, electronic games or transmitting devices, including radio-controlled toys and walkie-talkies. The use of devices that use Wi-Fi or Bluetooth is prohibited during take-off and landing. During the rest of the flight, these devices may be used in a manner which does not interfere with the aircraft's navigation and communication systems e.g., in airplane mode. Operation of hearing aids and heart pacemakers which do not interfere with the navigation or communication system of the aircraft on which it is to be operated and for which such operator has obtained relevant approval is permitted. 
(e). The Government of India prohibits serving alcohol on the domestic flights and smoking in any form on all flights. As a separate precautionary measure, all toilets are fitted with smoke detectors. Tampering with or disabling the smoke detector is prohibited. The use of e-cigarettes or any other vaping device is not permitted on board the aircraft. 
(f). Passengers shall note that any act (attempted or otherwise) of removal or tampering with any safety equipment on the aircraft is prohibited.
(g). The Government of India regulations do not permit photography at defence airports (except the civil enclaves at defence airport) and special permission is required to be taken in accordance with Applicable Laws. Any photography/videography which includes use of any recording equipment which imperils or compromises air safety, violates prevalent norms, creates chaos or disruption during operation of the flight or is expressly prohibited by the aircraft crew, will not be permitted on all AIXL flights. Restricted photography is permitted as per the notifications and guidelines released by the appropriate regulatory authority from time to time. Please visit the website of the DGCA for further details.

# SpiceJet - Low Cost Air Travel, International Flight Tickets from India, Cheap Airline Tickets India | SpiceJet Airlines

- Archive Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20240601000000/https://corporate.spicejet.com/Tnc.aspx

TERMS OF CARRIAGE
f
Domestic
International
Interline

The definitions listed below apply to the terms mentioned across the Domestic and International Terms of Carriage or other pages on the website.

Passenger: Any person, except members of the crew, carried or to be carried in an aircraft pursuant to a Ticket.
SG: It’s a SpiceJet designator code. Such codes identify particular air carriers and in the case of SpiceJet Limited, SG denotes or means SpiceJet Limited.
Adult: For the purpose of buying a Ticket or for Tariff purposes, a person who has reached his/her 12th birthday or completed 12 years of age as of the date of commencement of travel.
ADF: The applicable Airport Development Fee collected by SpiceJet per passenger per sector on behalf of the airport operator(s).
Aircraft: A machine that can travel through air and has been certified as airworthy by the certified competent aeronautical authority.
ATO: The Airport Ticketing Office situated at the airport.
Agreed Stopping Places: Those places, except the place of departure and the place of destination, set out in the Ticket or shown in the airlines’ timetables as scheduled stopping places on the Passenger’s route.
Authorized Agent: A sales agent who has been appointed by SpiceJet to represent the airline in the sale of air transportation on its services.
Baggage: Refers to the passengers' personal property accompanying them in connection with their trip. Unless otherwise specified, it consists of both their checked and hand baggage.
Baggage Check: A check of passengers’ baggage to ensure that they contain no item that is dangerous or illegal or prohibited for carriage.
Baggage Identification Tag: A document issued solely for the identification of Checked Baggage.
BCAS: It stands for the Bureau of Civil Aviation Security, Government of India.
Booking: An act of creating an itinerary, record or reservation, either in paper form or in electronic form, with passenger details such as name, contact information, etc., through SpiceJet’s reservation channels, of the travel particulars of a passenger on a given flight.
Carrier: An air carrier other than SpiceJet whose designator code appears on the passengers’ Ticket or on a Conjunction Ticket.
Conjunction Ticket: A ticket issued to a passenger concurrently with another ticket(s) which together constitute a single contract of carriage.
Checked Baggage: It’s the baggage that is in compliance with airline baggage regulations and delivered to the airline during check-in to be stored in an inaccessible area to the passenger during the flight, for which the airline issues a Baggage Identification Tag.
Check-in deadline: The deadline that SpiceJet sets for passengers to finish check-in procedures and obtain their boarding passes.
Child: Passenger who is over the age of 2 (two) years and under the age of 12 (twelve) years, as on the date of travel.
Chosen Partner: A travel agency or travel portal that makes bookings, issues tickets, and provides other ancillary services for or on behalf of SpiceJet.
Conditions of Contract: Those statements contained in or delivered with the passenger’s Ticket or itinerary or receipt, identified as such, and which incorporate, by reference, these terms/conditions of carriage and notices.
Convention: Whichever of the following instruments is applicable:
The Convention for the Unification of Certain Rules Relating to International Carriage by Air, signed at Warsaw on October 12, 1929 (hereinafter referred to as the Warsaw Convention);
The Warsaw Convention, as amended at The Hague on September 28, 1955;
The Warsaw Convention as amended by Additional Protocol No.1 of Montreal (1975);
The Warsaw Convention as amended at The Hague and by Additional Protocol No. 4 of Montreal (1975);
The Montreal Convention (1999)
Credit Shell: A credit note issued by SpiceJet to a Passenger, on account of any adjustment in the taxable value of services to be offered by SpiceJet and any compensation to be provided to Passengers under applicable law which may include redressal of any Passenger grievance in terms of the provisions of these terms/conditions of carriage.
Damage: Includes death, wounding, or bodily injury to a Passenger, loss, partial loss, theft, or other damage to Baggage arising out of or in connection with carriage or other services incidental thereto performed by SpiceJet.
Days: Calendar days, including all seven days of the week; provided that, for the purpose of notification, the day upon which notice is dispatched shall not be counted; and provided further that, for purposes of determining the duration of validity of a Ticket, the day upon which the Ticket is issued or the flight commenced shall not be counted.
Designator Code: The two or three characters or letters which identify particular air carriers in tickets, schedules, reservation systems, communications, etc. This code is assigned by IATA.
DGCA: Stands for the Directorate General of Civil Aviation, Government of India.
Fare Rules: The terms and conditions attached to the fare.
Fare: The amount charged by the Carrier for the carriage of a passenger and his allowable free baggage, which is paid as fee by a passenger for air transport to fly from an origin to destination and includes the conditions, rules and restrictions for travelling on the airfare, as being applicable to the class of service to be furnished to the public, also otherwise known as an airfare.
Fit to Fly Certificate: The certificate required to be obtained by certain travelers from a registered medical practitioner as indicated in these terms of carriage.
Force Majeure: Unusual and unforeseeable circumstances beyond SpiceJet’s control, the consequences of which could not have been avoided even if all due care had been exercised.
Gate No-show: A passenger who has checked in for an outbound flight but fails to report at the boarding gate within the requisite timelines prior to the departure of the outbound flight.
GST: Goods and service tax, which is an indirect tax leviable on the supply of goods and services and includes SGST, CGST, UTGST, IGST, or a combination thereof, and applicable cess.
GSTIN: A unique goods and services tax identification number issued to the person duly registered with the relevant government authority.
Hand Baggage: Any of the Passenger’s baggage other than Checked Baggage that the Passenger is permitted to carry with him or her on the flight in accordance with the terms and conditions and applicable laws, rules, and regulations.
Infant: A Passenger with age between 7days and below 2 years on the date of travel.
INR: Stands for Indian Rupees, which is the lawful currency of India.
Itinerary, Receipt, Ticket, or E-Ticket: A document or documents, whether physical or electronic, including the passenger's identity, flight details, conditions of contract, and notices that are provided by SpiceJet or on behalf of SpiceJet to travelers who are flying with the airline.
No-show: A passenger who has made a booking but fails to check in for their outbound flight within the requisite timelines prior to departure and fails to cancel their booking.
Pets or Live Animals (AVI): Domesticated dogs.
PNR: A passenger name record, which is a unique booking reference number which identifies the passenger's booking in SpiceJet’s database for a sector or combination of sectors.
PSF or Passenger Service Fee: The applicable passenger service fee collected by SpiceJet per passenger per sector on behalf of the airport operator(s).
Regulatory Authority: Any statutory, government, regulatory and/or quasi-judiciary commission, court, body or authority (either at the union, state, or local level) incorporated under a statute or functioning within the purview of applicable laws.
Reservation Centre: SpiceJet’s 24*7 centre that helps in booking, modifying, or cancelling the flight ticket, along with other queries that a passenger may have regarding air travel. Contact numbers: +91 (0)124 4983410, +91 (0)124 7101600.
Sector: Each consecutive flight segment that has the same flight number.
Stopover: A scheduled stop on the passenger’s journey at a point between the place of departure and the place of destination.
Tariff: The published fares, charges and/or related conditions of carriage of an airline filed, where required, with the appropriate authorities.
Terms of Carriage: Conditions that form a legally binding and enforceable contract of carriage between SpiceJet and a passenger, that are available on the website and are incorporated by reference in the itinerary issued to passengers for bookings made through the website or through travel agents. The terms of carriage shall be subject to change from time to time, based on applicable law or at SpiceJet’s sole discretion.
UDF: The User Development Fee, as imposed by the relevant airport authority at certain airports in India and as applicable at the time of issuance of a ticket.
Unaccompanied Minor: A passenger between the ages of 5 (five) and 12 (twelve) years on the date of travel who is not accompanied by a passenger aged 18 (eighteen) years or more on the date of travel.
Website: Refers to the official website of SpiceJet, that is, spicejet.com, on which passengers can purchase tickets and also access information about the said airline, its offerings, and terms of carriage.

Terms of Carriage

The carriage of a Passenger is subject to SpiceJet regulations relating to the conditions of Non-International Carriage (Passenger and Baggage) framed in accordance with The Carriage by Air Act, 1972 and Notification regarding application of the Carriage which is non-international. These regulations are known as SpiceJet Non-International Carriage (passenger and baggage) Regulations 1992. The liability of the company for damage sustained in the event of the death or wounding of a passenger or any other bodily injury suffered by a passenger or by his registered baggage during the course of carriage by air will be governed by the provisions of sections 4,5,6 and the rules contained in the Second Schedule of Carriage by Air Act 1972 with certain exceptions, adaptations, modifications, etc. as notified in the Govt. of India, Ministry of Civil Aviation Notification and as amended from time to time. All disputes shall be subject to jurisdiction of Delhi only.

SpiceJet is a ticketless airline. An itinerary does not constitute a document of carriage. The Booking in the SpiceJet database is the primary record of carriage and in the event of any differences between the itinerary and the Booking in the SpiceJet database, the Booking will prevail.

All Passengers, including children and infants, must present valid identification at check-in. It is your responsibility to ensure you have the appropriate travel documents at all times.
All Foreign Nationals/Non-Indian Nationals/NRI need to carry their Passport with valid documents for their travel to Port Blair(Andaman and Nicobar Island). All NRI must have PIO(person of indian origin) or Passport with valid documents. As Andaman and Nicobar Islands being the Restricted Area under Foreign Nationals (Restricted) Order 1963, hence the provision of Restricted Area Permit (RAP) has been relaxed for the visit by Foreigners to 30 islands in A & N Islands. However, the citizens of China, Afghanistan & Pakistan and those who have origin in these countries and citizens of Myanmar intending to visit Mayabunder & Diglipur in North & Middle Andaman District continue to require prior approval of Ministry of Home Affairs to gain entry and avoid any inconvenience.
Web check-in is available for all domestic flights and closes 60 mins prior to departure. For assistance with check-in or re-issuance of boarding pass through Reservations, a facilitation fee of Rs. 200 per passenger will be charged. Bookings made under the fares of armed forces, senior citizens, unaccompanied minors and for passengers with medical conditions/stretchers are exempted from this fee. Check-in counters will open three hours prior to departure and will close 60 mins prior to departure. Passengers are requested to report to the check-in counter at least two hours prior to departure
Cancellation / Changes within "2 hours" prior to the scheduled departure time or failure to check-in for a SpiceJet flight at least 60 minutes prior, to the scheduled departure time will result in the fare being forfeited.
All promo/sale fares are restrictive fares and are non-refundable. Certain promo/sale fares do not permit changes to the flight. Please check restrictions on the fare while booking. Under all promo/sale fares, limited inventory is available on selected flights on first come, first served basis. SpiceJet reserves the right to withdraw and/or amend the promo/sale without any prior notice.
In the event of cancellation/non-utilization/no show of promo/special fares (where the basic fare is non-refundable), the passengers shall be entitled for the refund of statutory taxes and User Development Fee (UDF) / Airport Development Fee (ADF) / Passenger Service Fee (PSF) etc (as applicable).However, on bookings made on flights to/from Ajmer, Belagavi, Durgapur, Gwalior, Jaisalmer, Jalandhar, Jharsuguda, Kandla, Kanpur, Pondicherry, Darbhanga and Porbandar do not qualify for same as taxes are not being collected on the said routes.
Cancellation, changes and refund
Spicejet shall provide “Look-in option” for a period of 24 hours after booking ticket. During this period passenger can cancel or amend the ticket without any additional charges, except for the normal prevailing fare for the revised flight for which the ticket is sought to be amended. This facility shall not be available for a flight whose departure is less than 7 days from booking date. The passenger needs to call SpiceJet’s call center to avail this facility.
For all domestic sectors any changes pertaining to Date for a booking please refer the grid below for applicable charges if the same fare is not available at the time of change, the difference in fares will be applied in addition to the change fee plus changes to any applicable fees. All fees are subject to change without notice.
For booking cancellations and flight changes requested via SpiceJet Reservations or airport ticketing counters, an additional sum of Rs.250 per passenger per flight will be chargeable.
For all domestic sectors any request for sector change in the booking will attract the respective cancellation fees as per the class of booking or base fare plus fuel surcharge per passenger per sector per change, whichever is lower. If the same fare is not available at the time of change, the difference in fares will be applied in addition to this change fee plus changes to any applicable fees. All fees are subject to change without notice.
If payment is made through the website using debit or credit cards, Net Banking, Wallets, or UPI, any refunds resulting from cancellations will be processed within seven (7) working days and credited back to the source account.
In case of cash transactions, refund shall be made via online bank transfer only.
If you cancel tickets that were purchased through travel agents, online travel portals, or similar platforms, the refund will be processed within seven (7) working days from the time of ticket cancellation.
Add on service like Meals, Spice-Max , Excess Baggage and Preferred Bag Out are non-cancellable in isolation.

At the end of the booking process, you can make the payment using the “CREDIT SHELL” option. Each passenger is permitted to carry one piece of hand baggage with maximum weight of 7 kg., free of cost. Hand baggage size must be within the dimensions of: 55 cm + 35 cm + 25 cm (L+W+H; total 115 cm) on Boeing flights and 50 cm + 35 cm + 23 cm (L+W+H; total 108 cm or 42.5 inches) on Q400 flights.

Laptop bag/ ladies purse/ duty free shopping bags can be carried additionally, as long as the total weight of cabin baggage does not exceed 7 kg.

Hand baggage over and above the permissible carriage limit of 7 kg will be charged at a cost of Rs.600 per kg.

Passengers with infants are permitted to carry an additional piece of hand baggage with maximum weight of 7 kg., and not exceeding the aforementioned size dimensions.

14.1

The issue relating to carriage of Kirpan by Sikh passengers, while traveling by air, has been reviewed in the light of requirements of maintenance of public order. It is decided that Kirpan may be carried under the following conditions :-

Kirpan may be carried only by a Sikh passenger, on his person, provided the length of its blade does not exceed 15.24 cms.(6 inches); and the total length of a Kirpan does not exceed 22.86 cms. ( 9 inches ) ;

It is allowed while traveling by air on Indian aircrafts within India; and

Kirpan is allowed only on domestic routes of fully domestic flights.

Hand Baggage will be accepted in cabin subject to the availability of space in the overhead bin. If the Hand baggage is oversized/ overweight, SpiceJet will accept it as Checked-in Baggage. Customer’s Hand Baggage will be specifically tagged and upon arrival the same will be available to be collected from the arrival hall conveyor belt. If the airline staff detects the passenger carrying excess hand baggage before and/ or at the time of boarding the aircraft, then he/she shall be charged INR 600/ kg for each additional kg, above 7kg free hand baggage allowance.

Passengers are kindly advised to place Liquids, Aerosols, and Gels (LAGs) containers within a transparent re-sealable plastic bag, with a maximum capacity not exceeding one litre. The recommended dimensions for the one-litre bag are approximately 20.5 cm x 20.5 cm or 25 cm x 15 cm, or their equivalent. Compliance with the Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016, and any subsequent amendments is expected regarding other specifications for such plastic bags. The containers are required to comfortably fit within the bag, which should be fully sealed. The provision of these plastic bags at security screening checkpoints for passenger use will be facilitated by the airport operator of the relevant airport.
